summary: cpu-sec-bench's scheduler could not distinguish a case it never ran - one deliberately unrunnable on the current platform, or one whose build failed - from a genuine test outcome, because a failed build recorded make's raw exit status as the case's result. This plan adds a scheduler-owned result code 1025 meaning not run, a per-record skip and skip-reason declaration matched against a CSB_TARGET_ARCH define the Makefile passes from ARCH after its feature-forcing blocks, a make-status sub-field in results.json carrying the raw build status, and two count lines in results.dat that report skipped and unbuildable records separately so lost coverage is never silent. It also adds a disable_independent_assembly build switch so a port can come up before its independent-assembly source is translated, and repairs two pre-existing defects the work surfaced: report_gen's sys-info header copy could loop forever and fill the disk, and cfi/return-to-peer-vfunc.cpp was missing the include that current g++ requires for uintptr_t. Files changed are scheduler/run-test.cpp, the Makefile, that one test-case source, and the README, doc/architecture.html, doc/porting.html and CLAUDE.md documentation set. The chief trade-off is that no skip declarations ship in configure.json: the mechanism is exercised through scratch registries, and the affected architectures stay covered by the opt-out plus automatic build-failure recording until the independent-assembly translation is finished.

Initialized Claude tooling, a browsable HTML documentation tree and repo hygiene for the public cpu-sec-bench repository, which previously had no CLAUDE.md, no working area and no browsable docs. The plan created a root CLAUDE.md guide covering rules, structure, commands and scheduler architecture; a declaration of the audit-relevant planner-owned locations at .claude/mega-audit-files.json; and a five-file doc/ tree holding a landing page, an architecture page documenting the scheduler algorithm, the configure.json field set and the nine-group exit-code contract, a curated catalog of all 246 records over 103 programs, a porting guide and a shared stylesheet. The catalog is guarded by a committed two-way set-equality check, script/check_catalog.py, chosen over generating the page from configure.json so that no generator or build step is added; it was renamed from check_test_catalog.py after that basename collided with a coder deny rule. Repo hygiene: .gitignore now ignores /tmp/, /.codegraph/ and /trace-log/ so machine-local working directories can never be committed, and the Makefile's dead LaTeX-era doc target was removed. README.md gained doc and plans entries plus the previously missing 64-65 result-code row, while INTERNAL.md's factual drift was declared and left unfixed as out of scope. Three issues remain deferred: the run-test continue variables.json defect, eight pre-existing scheduler compiler warnings, and hardening of the catalog guard.
